allow_large: Two code files plus tests, a decision record and synced skill copies; under the rule already on main (tests and sync output don't count) it is within the limit, but the installed release still counts them
done_when: Before each Codex thread start or resume, Forge asks the app-server for the checkout's project hooks; each hook whose definition is exactly what forge sync writes for this repo is passed to the turn as trusted (its current hash in the thread config's hooks state), so the guard and the other Forge hooks run on every worker and reader turn; if any project hook is not trusted and differs from Forge's own, the turn stops with one plain line naming the hook and how to review it in Codex's /hooks, changing nothing. Decision 0102 records the owner's choice and supersedes decision 0082 for Forge's own hooks. Command-level tests with the stub app-server: Forge's own untrusted hooks are trusted and the turn starts with them; a modified or foreign untrusted hook stops the turn.

findings.body: The stub reads hooks from the worktree, while new dependency evidence in [Codex 0.159.2's loader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs) shows that linked worktrees use main-checkout hook declarations (`root_checkout_hooks_folder_for_dir` and `merge_root_checkout_project_hooks`). The new worker and reader tests sync and modify only worktree hooks, so their positive and refusal cases exercise a different hook source from production. Make the stub follow this contract and update fresh/resumed worker and reader fixtures to modify the hooks Codex actually loads.
findings.title: Not done: Hook-trust command tests model Codex's worktree hook source

findings.body: All four new regression tests use Forge-source fixtures. `_codex_repo` defaults to `client=False` (`tests/test_codex_worker.py:110–128`), and the reader's `setup` and `_toml` helpers also default to `forge-source` (`tests/test_story.py:67`, `tests/test_codex_worker.py:102`). None exercises this behavior after client init/adoption or after upgrading an existing client adopted on the previous release. The repository's explicit review rule requires both. Extend the command-level proof to those client lifecycles, checking Forge-hook trust and modified/foreign-hook refusal.
findings.title: Not done: Hook trust in new and upgraded client repos

findings.body: The previously reported gap remains: `src/forge/doctor.py:75–82` accepts either checkout or main-repository trust, even when the checkout is explicitly untrusted. [Codex's trust resolver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/refs/tags/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs) gives the checkout's explicit decision precedence. Forge therefore proceeds while Codex excludes project hooks, leaving workers, readers and `forge ask` without the guard. The stub repeats the permissive check at `tests/stubs/codex-app-server:97–100`. Honor explicit checkout distrust before inheriting repository trust and cover conflicting entries through a Forge command.
findings.title: Respect explicit worktree distrust before inheriting repository trust
